title: The plus construction is a presheaf, and its elements and equalities are described by refinements
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a site [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], $\mathcal F$ a presheaf of sets on $\mathcal C$, and $H^0(\mathcal U,\mathcal F)$, morphisms of coverings, $\mathcal F^+(U)=\operatorname{colim}_{\mathcal J_U^{opp}}H^0(\mathcal U,\mathcal F)$, the classes $[\mathcal U,s]$, the maps $\mathcal F^+(h)$ and $\theta$ as in [def-weil-pbc-site-plus-construction]. Then: (1) every element of $\mathcal F^+(U)$ is of the form $[\mathcal U,s]$ for some covering $\mathcal U$ of $U$ and some $s\in H^0(\mathcal U,\mathcal F)$; (2) for coverings $\mathcal U,\mathcal U'$ of $U$ and $s\in H^0(\mathcal U,\mathcal F)$, $s'\in H^0(\mathcal U',\mathcal F)$ one has $[\mathcal U,s]=[\mathcal U',s']$ if and only if there are a covering $\mathcal V$ of $U$ and morphisms of coverings $f:\mathcal V\to\mathcal U$, $f':\mathcal V\to\mathcal U'$ over $\mathrm{id}_U$ with $f^*s=f'^*s'$ in $H^0(\mathcal V,\mathcal F)$; in particular, for $a,b\in\mathcal F(U)$, $\theta_U(a)=\theta_U(b)$ if and only if there is a covering $\{V_k\to U\}$ with $a|_{V_k}=b|_{V_k}$ for all $k$; (3) for every morphism $h:V\to U$, every covering $\mathcal U$ of $U$, every covering $\mathcal W$ of $V$ and every morphism of coverings $g:\mathcal W\to\mathcal U$ lying over $h$, one has $\mathcal F^+(h)([\mathcal U,s])=[\mathcal W,g^*s]$ for all $s\in H^0(\mathcal U,\mathcal F)$; in particular the maps $\mathcal F^+(h)$ do not depend on the chosen fibre products, and if $\mathcal U=\{U_i\to U\}_{i\in I}$ and $h$ factors as $V\xrightarrow{c}U_i\to U$ for some $i$, then $\mathcal F^+(h)([\mathcal U,s])=\theta_V(s_i|_V)$ with $s_i|_V=\mathcal F(c)(s_i)$; (4) with these maps $\mathcal F^+$ is a presheaf of sets on $\mathcal C$ ($\mathcal F^+(\mathrm{id}_U)=\mathrm{id}$ and $\mathcal F^+(h\circ k)=\mathcal F^+(k)\circ\mathcal F^+(h)$) and $\theta:\mathcal F\to\mathcal F^+$ is a morphism of presheaves.

source.place: Sites, Section 00W1: Lemma 00W4 (lemma-plus-presheaf) for (4); Lemma 00W6 (lemma-common-refinement), Lemma 00W7 (lemma-independent-refinement) and the paragraph after Remark 00W8 (the diagram is filtered; description of elements and equality in the colimit) for (1), (2); the remark after Lemma 00W4 and the proof of Lemma 00W9 (lemma-plus-surjective) for (3)

proof.text: *The colimit is a filtered colimit over the coverings ordered by refinement.* Fix $U$ and let $D_U:\mathcal J_U^{opp}\to$ sets, $\mathcal U\mapsto H^0(\mathcal U,\mathcal F)$, $f\mapsto f^*$, with colimit $(\mathcal F^+(U),(\iota_{\mathcal U}))$, $\iota_{\mathcal U}(s)=[\mathcal U,s]$ [def-weil-pbc-site-plus-construction] (c). The category $\mathcal J_U^{opp}$ itself need not be filtered (two different morphisms of coverings $\mathcal V\to\mathcal U$ need not be equalized by precomposition); following Stacks (the diagram is filtered in the sense of Categories, Definition 002V, and the footnote there) we pass to the preorder. Let $P_U$ be the category whose objects are the coverings of $U$, with exactly one morphism $\mathcal V\to\mathcal U$ if $\mathcal V$ refines $\mathcal U$ (there is a morphism $\mathcal V\to\mathcal U$ in $\mathcal J_U$) and none otherwise; it is a small category, since refinement is reflexive (identity morphism of coverings) and transitive (composition of morphisms of coverings over $\mathrm{id}_U$) [def-weil-pbc-site-plus-construction] (b), and the coverings of $U$ form a set [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]. By [lem-weil-pbc-site-covering-morphisms-same-h0-map], all morphisms $f:\mathcal V\to\mathcal U$ in $\mathcal J_U$ induce one and the same map $\rho_{\mathcal V\mathcal U}=f^*:H^0(\mathcal U,\mathcal F)\to H^0(\mathcal V,\mathcal F)$; since $(g\circ f)^*=f^*g^*$ and $\mathrm{id}^*=\mathrm{id}$ [def-weil-pbc-site-plus-construction] (b), $D'_U:P_U^{opp}\to$ sets, $\mathcal U\mapsto H^0(\mathcal U,\mathcal F)$, $(\mathcal V\le\mathcal U)\mapsto\rho_{\mathcal V\mathcal U}$, is a functor with $D_U=D'_U\circ q$ for the evident functor $q:\mathcal J_U^{opp}\to P_U^{opp}$ (identity on objects). A family of maps $\mu_{\mathcal U}:H^0(\mathcal U,\mathcal F)\to M$ is a cocone on $D_U$ iff $\mu_{\mathcal V}f^*=\mu_{\mathcal U}$ for every morphism $f:\mathcal V\to\mathcal U$ of $\mathcal J_U$, iff $\mu_{\mathcal V}\rho_{\mathcal V\mathcal U}=\mu_{\mathcal U}$ whenever $\mathcal V$ refines $\mathcal U$, iff it is a cocone on $D'_U$. So $D_U$ and $D'_U$ have the same cocones, and $(\mathcal F^+(U),(\iota_{\mathcal U}))$, a colimit of $D_U$, is a colimit of $D'_U$ [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit] (the factorization property is the same condition). Finally $P_U^{opp}$ is filtered [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]: it has the object $\{\mathrm{id}_U\}$ (axiom (i) of a site); two coverings $\mathcal U,\mathcal U'$ of $U$ have a common refinement $\mathcal W$ with morphisms $\mathcal W\to\mathcal U$, $\mathcal W\to\mathcal U'$ over $\mathrm{id}_U$ [lem-weil-pbc-site-coverings-common-refinement], i.e. arrows $\mathcal U\to\mathcal W$, $\mathcal U'\to\mathcal W$ in $P_U^{opp}$; and two parallel arrows of $P_U^{opp}$ are equal.

source.place: Sites, Section 00W1: the paragraph after Remark 00W8 ('From these two lemmas, and the fact that J_U is nonempty, it follows that the diagram H^0(-,F): J_U^opp -> Sets is filtered'), using Lemmas 00W6 and 00W7; literature/stacks-project/categories.tex, Definition 002V and the footnote after it (passing to the quotient index category)

proof.text: *Clauses (1) and (2).* Apply [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-sets-elementwise] to the filtered category $P_U^{opp}$ and the functor $D'_U$ with colimit $(\mathcal F^+(U),(\iota_{\mathcal U}))$ (Step 1). Its clause (1) says every element of $\mathcal F^+(U)$ is $\iota_{\mathcal U}(s)=[\mathcal U,s]$ for a covering $\mathcal U$ of $U$ and $s\in H^0(\mathcal U,\mathcal F)$: this is (1). Its clause (2) says $[\mathcal U,s]=[\mathcal U',s']$ iff there is an object $\mathcal V$ of $P_U^{opp}$ with arrows $\mathcal U\to\mathcal V$, $\mathcal U'\to\mathcal V$ in $P_U^{opp}$ such that $\rho_{\mathcal V\mathcal U}(s)=\rho_{\mathcal V\mathcal U'}(s')$; an arrow $\mathcal U\to\mathcal V$ of $P_U^{opp}$ means that there is a morphism of coverings $f:\mathcal V\to\mathcal U$ over $\mathrm{id}_U$, and then $\rho_{\mathcal V\mathcal U}=f^*$ for every such $f$ (Step 1). Hence $[\mathcal U,s]=[\mathcal U',s']$ iff there are a covering $\mathcal V$ of $U$ and morphisms of coverings $f:\mathcal V\to\mathcal U$, $f':\mathcal V\to\mathcal U'$ over $\mathrm{id}_U$ with $f^*s=f'^*s'$: this is the main assertion of (2).

source.place: Sites, Section 00W1, the paragraph after Remark 00W8 ('every element in the set F^+(U) arises from an element s in H^0(U,F) ... s and s' determine the same element of the colimit if and only if there exists a covering V of U and refinements f, f' such that f^*s = (f')^*s''); Categories, Section 04AX

proof.text: *The case of $\theta$ in (2).* Let $a,b\in\mathcal F(U)$, so $\theta_U(a)=[\{\mathrm{id}_U\},a]$, $\theta_U(b)=[\{\mathrm{id}_U\},b]$ with $H^0(\{\mathrm{id}_U\},\mathcal F)=\mathcal F(U)$ [def-weil-pbc-site-plus-construction] (c). For a covering $\mathcal V=\{v_k:V_k\to U\}_{k\in K}$, a morphism of coverings $f:\mathcal V\to\{\mathrm{id}_U\}$ over $\mathrm{id}_U$ consists of the unique map $K\to\{*\}$ and morphisms $f_k:V_k\to U$ with $\mathrm{id}_U\circ f_k=\mathrm{id}_U\circ v_k$, i.e. $f_k=v_k$; so there is exactly one such morphism, and $(f^*a)_k=\mathcal F(v_k)(a)=a|_{V_k}$ [def-weil-pbc-site-plus-construction] (b). By the main assertion of (2) (Step 2) with $\mathcal U=\mathcal U'=\{\mathrm{id}_U\}$: $\theta_U(a)=\theta_U(b)$ iff there is a covering $\mathcal V=\{V_k\to U\}$ of $U$ (the morphisms $f,f'$ to $\{\mathrm{id}_U\}$ then exist and are equal) with $f^*a=f^*b$, i.e. $a|_{V_k}=b|_{V_k}$ for all $k$.

source.place: Sites, Section 00W1, the paragraph after Remark 00W8, specialized to the trivial covering {id_U} (used in the proof of Theorem 00WB(2))

proof.text: *Clause (3), the formula.* Let $h:V\to U$, $\mathcal U=\{\pi_i:U_i\to U\}_{i\in I}$, $\mathcal W=\{w_l:W_l\to V\}_{l\in L}$ a covering of $V$, and $g=(h,\gamma,(g_l)_{l\in L}):\mathcal W\to\mathcal U$ a morphism of coverings over $h$, so $\pi_{\gamma(l)}g_l=h\,w_l$. By definition [def-weil-pbc-site-plus-construction] (c), $\mathcal F^+(h)[\mathcal U,s]=[\mathcal U\times_UV,p_{\mathcal U}^*s]$ with the chosen fibre products $U_i\times_UV$ and $p_{\mathcal U}=(h,\mathrm{id}_I,(\mathrm{pr}_1)_i)$. Since $\pi_{\gamma(l)}g_l=h\,w_l$, the universal property of $U_{\gamma(l)}\times_UV$ gives a unique $k_l:W_l\to U_{\gamma(l)}\times_UV$ with $\mathrm{pr}_1k_l=g_l$ and $\mathrm{pr}_2k_l=w_l$. Then $k=(\mathrm{id}_V,\gamma,(k_l)):\mathcal W\to\mathcal U\times_UV$ is a morphism of coverings over $\mathrm{id}_V$ (the condition is $\mathrm{pr}_2k_l=\mathrm{id}_V w_l$), i.e. a morphism of $\mathcal J_V$, and $p_{\mathcal U}\circ k=(h\,\mathrm{id}_V,\gamma,(\mathrm{pr}_1k_l))=(h,\gamma,(g_l))=g$ (composition of morphisms of coverings, [def-weil-pbc-site-plus-construction] (b)). Hence $g^*s=k^*p_{\mathcal U}^*s$ by functoriality of $(-)^*$ [def-weil-pbc-site-plus-construction] (b), and by the cocone property of the coprojections $\iota^V$ of $\mathcal F^+(V)$ for the morphism $k$ of $\mathcal J_V$ [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit], $[\mathcal W,g^*s]=\iota^V_{\mathcal W}(k^*p_{\mathcal U}^*s)=\iota^V_{\mathcal U\times_UV}(p_{\mathcal U}^*s)=\mathcal F^+(h)[\mathcal U,s]$.

source.place: Sites, Section 00W1, the remark after Lemma 00W4 ('we may pullback an element s as above via any morphism from any covering of W to {U_i -> U} and we will always end up with the same element'); written out by the agent, without Lemma 00W7, from the construction of F^+(h) before Lemma 00W4

proof.text: *Clause (3), independence of the fibre products and the factorization case.* If $U_i\times'_UV$ is another choice of fibre products, with projections $\mathrm{pr}'_1,\mathrm{pr}'_2$, then $\mathcal U\times'_UV=\{U_i\times'_UV\to V\}$ is a covering of $V$ (the canonical isomorphisms $\phi_i:U_i\times'_UV\to U_i\times_UV$ over $V$ give coverings $\{\phi_i\}$ by axiom (i), and composing them with the covering $\mathcal U\times_UV$ gives a covering by axiom (ii) [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]) and $p'_{\mathcal U}=(h,\mathrm{id}_I,(\mathrm{pr}'_1))$ is a morphism of coverings over $h$; by Step 4, $[\mathcal U\times'_UV,p'^*_{\mathcal U}s]=\mathcal F^+(h)[\mathcal U,s]$, so the map defined with the other choices agrees with $\mathcal F^+(h)$ on every class, hence everywhere by (1) (Step 2). Factorization case: if $h=\pi_i\circ c$ with $c:V\to U_i$, then $\{\mathrm{id}_V\}$ is a covering of $V$ (axiom (i)) and $g=(h,\,*\mapsto i,\,c):\{\mathrm{id}_V\}\to\mathcal U$ is a morphism of coverings over $h$, the condition being $\pi_ic=h\,\mathrm{id}_V$; $g^*s=\mathcal F(c)(s_i)=s_i|_V\in H^0(\{\mathrm{id}_V\},\mathcal F)=\mathcal F(V)$, so by Step 4 $\mathcal F^+(h)[\mathcal U,s]=[\{\mathrm{id}_V\},s_i|_V]=\theta_V(s_i|_V)$ [def-weil-pbc-site-plus-construction] (c).

source.place: Sites, Section 00W1: footnote to the construction of F^+(V) -> F^+(U) ('The resulting map does not depend on the choices made, see below') and the proof of Lemma 00W9 (lemma-plus-surjective: the morphism of coverings {U_i -> U_i} -> {U_i -> U} computes the restriction as theta(s_i))

proof.text: *Clause (4).* Identity: the identity $(\mathrm{id}_U,\mathrm{id}_I,(\mathrm{id}_{U_i}))$ of $\mathcal U$ is a morphism of coverings over $\mathrm{id}_U$ [def-weil-pbc-site-plus-construction] (b), so by Step 4 $\mathcal F^+(\mathrm{id}_U)[\mathcal U,s]=[\mathcal U,s]$; by (1) every element is such a class, so $\mathcal F^+(\mathrm{id}_U)=\mathrm{id}$. Composition: for $k:W\to V$, $h:V\to U$ and $[\mathcal U,s]\in\mathcal F^+(U)$, by definition $\mathcal F^+(k)\mathcal F^+(h)[\mathcal U,s]=\mathcal F^+(k)[\mathcal U\times_UV,p_{\mathcal U}^*s]=[(\mathcal U\times_UV)\times_VW,p_{\mathcal U\times_UV}^*p_{\mathcal U}^*s]=[(\mathcal U\times_UV)\times_VW,(p_{\mathcal U}\circ p_{\mathcal U\times_UV})^*s]$, and $p_{\mathcal U}\circ p_{\mathcal U\times_UV}$ is a morphism of coverings from the covering $(\mathcal U\times_UV)\times_VW$ of $W$ to $\mathcal U$ over $h\circ k$ (composites of morphisms of coverings lie over the composite, [def-weil-pbc-site-plus-construction] (b)); by Step 4 the last class is $\mathcal F^+(h\circ k)[\mathcal U,s]$. By (1), $\mathcal F^+(k)\circ\mathcal F^+(h)=\mathcal F^+(h\circ k)$, so $\mathcal F^+$ is a functor $\mathcal C^{op}\to$ sets. Naturality of $\theta$: for $h:V\to U$ and $a\in\mathcal F(U)=H^0(\{\mathrm{id}_U\},\mathcal F)$, $h$ factors as $\mathrm{id}_U\circ h$ through the single member of $\{\mathrm{id}_U\}$, so the factorization case of Step 5 gives $\mathcal F^+(h)(\theta_U(a))=\theta_V(\mathcal F(h)(a))$.

split_report.summary: Proof written in six steps from Stacks Sites Section 00W1, read against def-weil-pbc-site-plus-construction (chosen fibre products, F^+(U) the chosen colimit over J_U^opp, F^+(h) via p_U). Stacks says the diagram H^0(-,F) on J_U^opp is filtered in the sense of Categories 002V (condition (3) only up to the diagram), not that J_U^opp is a filtered category, so Step 1 passes to the refinement preorder P_U (Lemma 00W7, new node lem-weil-pbc-site-covering-morphisms-same-h0-map) with the same cocones, and uses the existing common refinement node (00W6) for filteredness; (1),(2) then follow from the existing Mathlib leaf lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-sets-elementwise; the theta case of (2) is the unique morphism of a covering to {id_U}. (3) is proved directly from the cocone property: any morphism of coverings g over h factors as p_U o k with k in J_V (no use of 00W7); independence of fibre products and the factorization case (00W9) follow. (4) from (1) and (3) (identity, composite of the p's lies over h o k, theta via the factorization case). Statement and stmt_deps kept; the Mathlib verdict (sieve-based plusObj, not a one-line specialization) confirmed and a grep of Plus.lean added.

reviewed.note: 6 steps following Stacks Sites 00W1: the colimit over J_U^opp equals the colimit over the refinement preorder, which is filtered by 00W6 (existing node) and 00W7 (new unsplit node: two morphisms of coverings over the same map induce the same map on H^0); (1),(2) from the elementwise description of filtered colimits of sets (leaf); the theta case; (3) via the factorization of any morphism of coverings over h through the chosen fibre-product covering and the cocone identity; independence of fibre products and the factorization case; (4) identity, composition, naturality. Tags verified.

lean.statement: theorem plus_construction_presheaf {C : Type u} [SmallCategory C] (J : Precoverage C) [J.HasIsos] [J.IsStableUnderComposition] [J.IsStableUnderBaseChange] [J.HasPullbacks] (P : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ Type (max u w)) : (∀ {U : C} (a : (J.toGrothendieck.plusObj P).obj (op U)), ∃ (E : Precoverage.ZeroHypercover.{max u w} J U) (x : Meq P ⟨E.sieve₀, J.generate_mem_toGrothendieck E.mem₀⟩), a = Plus.mk x) ∧ (∀ {U : C} (E F : Precoverage.ZeroHypercover.{max u w} J U) (x : Meq P ⟨E.sieve₀, J.generate_mem_toGrothendieck E.mem₀⟩) (y : Meq P ⟨F.sieve₀, J.generate_mem_toGrothendieck F.mem₀⟩), Plus.mk x = Plus.mk y ↔ ∃ (W : Precoverage.ZeroHypercover.{max u w} J U) (f : W ⟶ E) (g : W ⟶ F), ∀ i : W.I₀, P.map (f.h₀ i).op (x ⟨E.X (f.s₀ i), E.f (f.s₀ i), E.sieve₀_f _⟩) = P.map (g.h₀ i).op (y ⟨F.X (g.s₀ i), F.f (g.s₀ i), F.sieve₀_f _⟩)) ∧ (∀ {U : C} (a b : P.obj (op U)), (J.toGrothendieck.toPlus P).app (op U) a = (J.toGrothendieck.toPlus P).app (op U) b ↔ ∃ (E : Precoverage.ZeroHypercover.{max u w} J U), ∀ i : E.I₀, P.map (E.f i).op a = P.map (E.f i).op b) ∧ (∀ {V U : C} (h : V ⟶ U) (E : Precoverage.ZeroHypercover.{max u w} J U) (W : Precoverage.ZeroHypercover.{max u w} J V) (g : (W.toPreZeroHypercover.pushforward h).Hom E.toPreZeroHypercover) (x : Meq P ⟨E.sieve₀, J.generate_mem_toGrothendieck E.mem₀⟩) (y : Meq P ⟨W.sieve₀, J.generate_mem_toGrothendieck W.mem₀⟩), (∀ i : W.I₀, y ⟨W.X i, W.f i, W.sieve₀_f i⟩ = P.map (g.h₀ i).op (x ⟨E.X (g.s₀ i), E.f (g.s₀ i), E.sieve₀_f _⟩)) → (J.toGrothendieck.plusObj P).map h.op (Plus.mk x) = Plus.mk y) ∧ (∀ {V U : C} (E : Precoverage.ZeroHypercover.{max u w} J U) (x : Meq P ⟨E.sieve₀, J.generate_mem_toGrothendieck E.mem₀⟩) (i : E.I₀) (c : V ⟶ E.X i), (J.toGrothendieck.plusObj P).map (c ≫ E.f i).op (Plus.mk x) = (J.toGrothendieck.toPlus P).app (op V) (P.map c.op (x ⟨E.X i, E.f i, E.sieve₀_f i⟩)))
lean.note: Uses the dependency records: a small Precoverage site, Type-valued presheaf, ZeroHypercover covering families, and plusObj/toPlus for the generated topology. Meq on the sieve generated by a family is its canonical compatible-family extension; equality and restriction are stated componentwise on covering families. Functor and natural-transformation laws are already fields of plusObj and toPlus.
